title: Simultaneous small chunks of a simplicial model category
statement:
Use simplicial and combinatorial model categories, projective diagram models, and smallness as in [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], and Bergner cofibrancy as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. A chunk $U$ of a combinatorial simplicial model category $\mathcal A$ means a full simplicial subcategory with the following two closure properties, with choices functorial by simplicially enriched functors. For each finite family $X\to Y_i$ in $U$, its product map factors as a trivial cofibration $X\to Z$ followed by a fibration $Z\to\prod_iY_i$, with $Z\in U$. For each finite family $Y_i\to X$ in $U$, its coproduct map factors as a cofibration $\coprod_iY_i\to Z$ followed by a trivial fibration $Z\to X$, with $Z\in U$. Empty families are included. Put $U^{cf}=U\cap\mathcal A^{cf}$. For a small simplicial category $I$, an $I$-chunk is a chunk $U$ such that the full subcategory $U^I$ of diagrams with all values in $U$ is a chunk of the projective model category $\mathcal A^I$.

The full category $\mathcal A$ is an $I$-chunk of itself for every small $I$. Given a small family $(I_\alpha)$ of small cofibrant simplicial categories and a small full subcategory $V\subseteq\mathcal A$, there exists a small full subcategory $U\subseteq\mathcal A$ containing $V$ which is an $I_\alpha$-chunk for every $\alpha$. It can be chosen with the same essential image as $V$ in the ordinary homotopy category $\mathcal A[W^{-1}]$, where $W$ denotes its model weak equivalences.
